Subject: License health & surge resilience — need numbers for Olive Systems renewal

Neha / Marissa,

Quick heads-up: Olive Systems (DEAL-8471) is up for renegotiation mid-September. They had two unexpected production surges in July — tokens jumped ~42% on the 7/21 event and again on 7/29. They asked for a durable surge path and better SLA credit options during the renewal.

Can you pull a short usage snapshot (Q2 daily burn + burst days flagged) and a simple ops ROI table showing current unit costs vs. proposed committed pricing? The exec wants a concrete recommendation: 1) small commit bump + burst pool, or 2) 6-month stepped commit with a staged discount.

I attached the raw query output (csv stub). If we agree a default suggestion I'll draft the amendment language.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Growth
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: License health & surge resilience — need numbers for Olive Systems renewal

Thanks Karthik — pulling and consolidating now. Attaching a cleaned usage PDF (olive_usage_q2.pdf) and an ops ROI snapshot (ops_roi_snapshot.xlsx). Top-line observations:

- Baseline run-rate for Q2: 18.6M tokens/month (70% chat, 30% embeddings).
- Burst days (defined as >2.5x daily mean): 4 days in July; two accounted for backend batch jobs, two appear user-driven spikes.
- Current committed discount (annual) expires next month — they are effectively on a lower commit since they didn’t renew the extra tranche.

Recommendation (short):
- Option A (conservative): +20% commit, maintain current term, add 50k burst credit pool billed as-prepaid; no term change.
- Option B (aggressive, recommended if they want runway): 6-month stepped commit: +10% first 2 months, +20% next 2, +30% last 2; 12% blended discount off list for the six months, include 100k burst credit and a one-time onboarding rebate.

I can send the external summary to Sarah with these two options and ask for a quick sync. Thoughts?

Attachments: olive_usage_q2.pdf, ops_roi_snapshot.xlsx (stubs)

-Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — great working with you on this renewal. I wanted to share a short, actionable summary of your current usage and two concrete options to address the July surges so you have something to review ahead of a call.

Summary (Q2):
- Average: ~18.6M tokens/month
- Burst days flagged (July): 4 days (two job-driven; two user-driven)
- Current commit: expiring in mid-September (leaves them exposed to on-demand tier for spikes)

Option A — Conservative, low-risk- +20% committed tokens (flat for the next 12 months)- Add a 50k prepaid burst pool for unplanned spikes- No term length change- Minimal paperwork; fast to implement

Option B — Staged capacity + cost protection (recommended if you expect more load)- 6-month stepped commit (10% / 10% / 20% / 20% / 20% / 20%)- 100k prepaid burst pool + 1-time onboarding rebate- 12% blended discount for the 6-month period- Includes automatic routing to a dedicated burst lane (reduces tail latency during spikes)

Costs and ROI: see attached ops_roi_snapshot.xlsx for token-level arithmetic and a short forecast showing break-even at ~3 months if spikes repeat. I attached the cleaned usage PDF as well. (Files attached: olive_usage_q2.pdf, ops_roi_snapshot.xlsx)

Ask: are you available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (8/29) at 10:00 PT to walk through the numbers and which option feels best? If preferred, we can draft the amendment language and share for procurement review.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — appreciate the concise options and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before the sync: 

1) How does the burst pool billing work if we exhaust the prepaid burst? Is excess usage billed at the same committed rate or at on-demand pricing?
2) Can the stepped commit be paused or reduced if we don’t see the predicted growth? We prefer flexibility for Q4 planning.
3) On the 12% blended discount in Option B — is that applied across all token types (chat + embeddings) or only generation tokens?

We can do 10:00 PT tomorrow — I’ve added our procurement lead (procurement@olivesys.com) in cc. If you can answer the above two bullets in the meeting invite or the doc, that would save time.

Appreciate it — Sarah

--
Sarah Nguyen
Director, Product Operations
Olive Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@olivesys.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 contract review: capacity resilience & ops ROI

Sarah — quick responses ahead of the 10:00 PT sync: 

1) Burst pool billing: any prepaid burst is consumed first. If exhausted, excess is billed at the committed unit rate if you have a commit in place that covers the quantity; otherwise excess is billed at the on-demand rate. For Option B (stepped commit) excess above the current step is billed at the step’s committed rate for the month.

2) Stepped commit flexibility: we can include a pause clause allowing one-step rollback (reduce the next step by up to 10%) with 30 days notice. We usually allow one downward adjustment in the six-month window to accommodate Q4 planning; we can bake that into the amendment.

3) Discount application: the 12% blended discount applies to generation tokens (chat/LLM) and 6% for embeddings — we were conservative on embeddings given their higher compute footprint. We can make that explicit in the SOW.

Next operational steps (post-call):
- If Olive picks Option A, legal sends a one-page amendment (fast-turn) and we provision burst credits within 3 business days.
- If Olive picks Option B, we’ll draft the stepped-commit schedule + pause clause and circulate a redline (doc attached: proposed_amendment_draft.docx).

I’ll join the 10:00 PT call. Thanks everyone — see you then.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
